title: role-immersion-mini-sprint-and-evidence-runbook
summary: Working doc: a condensed 14-day immersion + evidence collection runbook for new hires in technical IC roles (platform, infra, serving-runtime). Goals: accelerate meaningful contributions, create repeatable interview->onboard alignment, and harvest observable evidence for early performance calibration.
hiring_goals: Hire 2 Platform Engineers (mid-senior) for Dedicated infra: primary focus on latency/observability work. Target competencies: low-level GPU infra familiarity, tracing/observability, deployment automation. Timeline: open reqs by 2026-02-28; final offers by 2026-03-21. Acceptance rate target 65% (improve via clearer role narrative and faster loop).
role_profile: Role shorthand: Platform Engineer (Dedicated). Day-to-day: own 1–2 feature slices (autoscale policies, model routing rules), support one oncall rotation, improve latency SLO telemetry. Must be comfortable with kernel/driver-adjacent troubleshooting, Python + Go, and reading CUDA/driver logs. Reports into platform-engineering. Seniority expectation: IC3-IC4 (3–7 years).
interview_rubric: Structure: 4 loop interviews + take-home. 1) System design (60m): evaluate large-scale routing, cache strategies; 2) Debug & triage (45m): live debugging of a failing batcher; 3) Coding (45m): medium algorithmic problem in Go/Python; 4) Culture & collaboration (30m): cross-team communication, shipping tradeoffs; 5) Take-home (optional for senior candidates): design a rollout/fallback plan for model sharding. Scoring: each loop 1–4 scale (1=unsafe, 4=exceeds). Must have no '1' in system design or triage. Evidence buckets we capture: tradeoff articulation, hypothesis-driven debugging steps, telemetry-first thinking, measurable impact estimates. Example probe questions included in appendix below.
onboarding_sprint_checklist: Orientation (Day 0-1): - HR & accounts: confirm SSO, KMS access request in HR-ops (ticket HR-OPS-18) - Slack intros: channel invites to #platform, #oncall - Hardware access: confirm VPN + internal lab scheduling First two days (Day 2-3): - Local dev setup: docker/gvisor images, internal model catalog clone - Shadow session: pair with buddy on an active incident (read-only) - Read: 'Serving runtime architecture' doc + 15 min sign-off quiz Day 4-7 (mini-project kickoff): - Mini-sprint planning: pick a 2-week micro-ticket (observability dashboard or small autoscale rule) - Deliverables: PR with tests gated for review within 5 working days - Weekly check-in: 30m with manager + 30m with cross-team owner Day 8-14 (evidence collection & demo): - Complete mini-ticket and ship to staging - Prepare 10-min demo: performance tradeoffs + measurement plan - Evidence pack: one page with links to PR, dashboards, test results, postmortem of any issues - Ramp criteria check: CI green, oncall readme updated, mentor sign-off Required artifacts to submit by day 14: (1) PR link, (2) runbook stub, (3) short post-demo slide deck (3 slides).
ramp_metrics: Qualitative: buddy feedback (scored 1-5), ability to lead a debugging session. Quantitative: PR throughput (>=1 merged meaningful PR in first 14 days), test coverage for micro-ticket (>=60% for touched modules), mean time to reproduce local incident <= 2 hours (guided). Longitudinal: readiness for independent oncall after 30 days as judged by SRE rota owner.
open_questions: - Do we require take-home for IC4+ or make it optional? (pros/cons noted) - Should we standardize the mini-sprint ticket templates across platform pods? (Ops vs. Product tradeoff) - Recruiter collateral: do we have a short 'day-in-life' slide for Dedicated infra? If not, create one. - Budget: hiring scorecard says 2 hires this quarter; fallback plan if only 1 hire: redistribute responsibilities and push backlog.
appendix_interview_probes: System design probes: - How would you design a model routing layer that selects between quantized and FP16 variants based on latency budget? Follow-ups: what telemetry would you collect? how to test canary? Debug & triage probes: - Given spike in tail-latency after a deployment, what first three checks do you run? (logs, KV cache hit rate, preemp events) Coding probes: - Implement a simple lock-free ring buffer snippet (pseudocode acceptable) Culture probes: - Describe a past tradeoff where you chose reliability over immediate user-facing feature. Take-home prompt (optional): - Draft a rollout plan that allows automatic fallback to a smaller-model shard when GPU memory pressure exceeds threshold. Expected deliverable: design doc + test plan.
